{\LARGE\bfseries\sffamily\color{AtlasNavy} Finite-arm lexicographic bandits without tradeoff side information\par}\vspace{5pt}


\textbf{Setting ID.} \texttt{ONX\_\allowbreak{}LEX\_\allowbreak{}FINITE\_\allowbreak{}UNKNOWN}



Online learning and bandits



Two-objective simultaneous regret when primary ties must be distinguished from small primary improvements without a supplied tradeoff bound.



\textbf{Status.} Logarithmic gap



\textbf{TASK tags.} solution concept: Lexicographic bandit regret; task family: Online bandit



\textbf{ORACLE tags.} feedback quality: Stochastic subgaussian; operation: Two coordinate reward vector; public information: Hidden objects explicitly declared; public information: Public inputs explicitly declared



\textbf{ALGORITHMS tags.} randomization: Private randomness allowed



\textbf{GUARANTEE tags.} aggregation: Per instance; mode: Expectation; mode: Probability; quantifier: Algorithm before instance



\textbf{RESOURCE tags.} measure: N arm pull; measure: N reward coordinate



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{1. Setting specification}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Task}


Minimize simultaneous coordinate regret for a two-objective lexicographic stochastic bandit without a supplied tradeoff envelope.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Admissible model}


The public action set is \AtlasInlineMath{[K]}, with the discrete metric \AtlasInlineMath{D(a,b)=\mathbf1\{a\ne b\}} and \AtlasInlineMath{K\ge2}.



There are two fixed reward means \AtlasInlineMath{\mu^1,\mu^2} taking values in \AtlasInlineMath{[0,1]}. The primary optimum set is \AtlasInlineMath{\mathcal X_1^*=\arg\max_x\mu^1(x)}, and a lexicographic optimum \AtlasInlineMath{x^*} maximizes \AtlasInlineMath{\mu^2} over that set. Primary ties are permitted.



The local tradeoff is \AtlasInlineMath{\lambda_* =\inf\{\lambda\ge0:\mu^2(x)-\mu^2(x^*)\le\lambda[\mu^1(x^*)-\mu^1(x)]\ \forall x\}}. No value or upper bound for \AtlasInlineMath{\lambda_*} is supplied. The same policy must handle all admissible means without such side information.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Oracle interface}


At round \AtlasInlineMath{t}, choose an arm \AtlasInlineMath{X_t} using the past and an independent random seed; then observe both coordinates \AtlasInlineMath{(Y_t^1,Y_t^2)}. Each coordinate is conditionally 1-sub-Gaussian around its fixed mean: \AtlasInlineMath{\mathbb E[\exp(\theta(Y_t^i-\mu^i(X_t)))\mid\mathcal H_{t-1},X_t]\le\exp(\theta^2/2)}. Independence between coordinates is not required. There is no feedback for unselected arms and no sample reuse interface.



The public inputs are \AtlasInlineMath{K,T} and, for a probability guarantee, \AtlasInlineMath{\delta}. The means and primary-optimal set are hidden.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Output}


The output is the sequence of selected arms. One policy must control both objective regrets against the same lexicographic optimum.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Loss or accuracy criterion}


Define \AtlasInlineMath{\Delta_i(x)=\mu^i(x^*)-\mu^i(x)} and signed coordinate regret \AtlasInlineMath{R_i(T)=\sum_{t=1}^T\Delta_i(X_t)}. The simultaneous expected criterion is \AtlasInlineMath{\max_{i\le2}\mathbb E R_i(T)}. The secondary regret can be negative, so the maximum is taken after each expectation.



For the high-probability view, use \AtlasInlineMath{R_i^+(T)=\sum_t[\Delta_i(X_t)]_+} and the common threshold for \AtlasInlineMath{\max_iR_i^+(T)}. This is a distinct metric linked to its explicit view.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Resource accounting}


There is one arm pull and two scalar reward observations per round, so the fixed horizon is \AtlasInlineMath{T}, the pull count is \AtlasInlineMath{T}, and the number of observed reward coordinates is \AtlasInlineMath{2T}. Computation and storage are unrestricted.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Algorithm views and success guarantees}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Simultaneous expected coordinate regret}


All measurable randomized nonanticipating policies are allowed. A policy may use K and T but no tradeoff envelope.




\AtlasMath{\forall\nu:\quad\max_{i\le2}\mathbb E_\nu R_i(T)\le r}




One policy handles every instance and both coordinates; the expectation includes observation and policy randomness.



\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_horizon



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{High-probability simultaneous positive regret}


All randomized nonanticipating policies may use K,T,delta, but no tradeoff envelope.




\AtlasMath{\forall\nu:\quad\Pr_\nu(\max_{i\le2}R_i^+(T)\le r)\ge1-\delta}




The same regret threshold must hold simultaneously for both objectives on every admissible instance.



Metric: The metric is \AtlasInlineMath{\max_{i\le2}R_i^+(T)} with \AtlasInlineMath{R_i^+(T)=\sum_t[\Delta_i(X_t)]_+}.



\textbf{Budget convention.} fixed\_horizon



\needspace{7\baselineskip}\section{2. Notation and parameters}


\AtlasInlineMath{K}: Number of arms \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{K\in\mathbb N_{\ge2}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{T}: Horizon \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{T\in\mathbb N_{\ge2}}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\delta}: Failure probability for the probability view \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0<\delta<1}.



\AtlasInlineMath{\lambda_*}: Instance local tradeoff; not given to the policy \textbf{Domain:} \AtlasInlineMath{0\le\lambda_*<\infty} on finite arm sets.



\needspace{12\baselineskip}\section{3. Complexity bracket}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{Compared quantities}


\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Q1 - minimax metric resource quantity}


\textbf{View.} Simultaneous expected coordinate regret



\AtlasMath{\mathfrak M_{T,K}=\inf_\pi\sup_{\nu\in\mathcal F_K}\max_{i\le2}\mathbb E_\nu R_i(T)}


\textbf{Scope.} The union of the explicit parameter and dimension domains of the linked comparison regimes; each bound retains its own applicability conditions.



\textbf{Optimization direction.} minimize



\textbf{Resource contract.} expression: \AtlasInlineMath{T}; description: Each played round and its prescribed feedback are charged.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsubsection{Q2 - minimax metric resource quantity}


\textbf{View.} High-probability simultaneous positive regret



\AtlasMath{\mathfrak Q_{T,K}(\delta)=\inf_\pi\inf\{r:\sup_{\nu\in\mathcal F_K}\Pr_\nu(\max_iR_i^+(T)>r)\le\delta\}}


\textbf{Scope.} The union of the explicit parameter and dimension domains of the linked comparison regimes; each bound retains its own applicability conditions.



\textbf{Optimization direction.} minimize



\textbf{Resource contract.} expression: \AtlasInlineMath{T}; description: Each played round and its prescribed feedback are charged.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{R1 - Expected regret without tradeoff side information}


\textbf{Region.} \AtlasInlineMath{K,T\ge2} integers; no tradeoff envelope is supplied. Finite action count K; no ambient Euclidean dimension.



\textbf{Views.} Simultaneous expected coordinate regret



\textbf{Quantity.} Q1



\textbf{Resource.} Each played round and its prescribed feedback are charged.



\textbf{Status.} Logarithmic gap



\textbf{Lower bound.} B2



\AtlasMath{\Omega\!\left(\min\{T,(K-1)^{1/3}T^{2/3}\}\right)}


\textbf{Upper bound.} B1



\AtlasMath{O\!\left(\min\{T,(K\log(4KT))^{1/3}T^{2/3}\}\right)}


\textbf{Gap or comparison.} At most an \AtlasInlineMath{O(\log^{1/3}(4KT))} factor remains.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{R2 - General finite-arm confidence dependence}


\textbf{Region.} \AtlasInlineMath{K\ge3}, \AtlasInlineMath{T\ge C} for the source universal threshold, and \AtlasInlineMath{0<\delta\le1/16}. Finite arm count K.



\textbf{Views.} High-probability simultaneous positive regret



\textbf{Quantity.} Q2



\textbf{Resource.} Each played round and its prescribed feedback are charged.



\textbf{Status.} Logarithmic gap



\textbf{Lower bound.} B4



\AtlasMath{\Omega\!\left(\min\{T,((K-1)\log(1/\delta))^{1/3}T^{2/3}\}\right)}


\textbf{Upper bound.} B3



\AtlasMath{O\!\left(\min\{T,(K\log(4K/\delta))^{1/3}T^{2/3}\}\right)}


\textbf{Gap or comparison.} The general-K upper bound has an additional factor of at most order \AtlasInlineMath{[\log(4K/\delta)/\log(1/\delta)]^{1/3}}.



\needspace{4\baselineskip}\subsection{R3 - Two-arm sharp confidence rate}


\textbf{Region.} \AtlasInlineMath{K=2}, \AtlasInlineMath{T\ge C} for the source universal threshold, and \AtlasInlineMath{0<\delta\le1/16}. Exactly two arms.



\textbf{Views.} High-probability simultaneous positive regret



\textbf{Quantity.} Q2



\textbf{Resource.} Each played round and its prescribed feedback are charged.



\textbf{Status.} Optimal



\textbf{Lower bound.} B6



\AtlasMath{\Omega\!\left(\min\{T,T^{2/3}\log^{1/3}(1/\delta)\}\right)}


\textbf{Upper bound.} B5



\AtlasMath{O\!\left(\min\{T,T^{2/3}\log^{1/3}(8/\delta)\}\right)}


\textbf{Gap or comparison.} The displayed logarithms differ by only constant factors throughout the stated delta range.
